desc: One thing about living abroad: your definition of 'normal' completely changes. My heart still skips a beat seeing these scooter rides. Would you trust your balance riding like this? #china #cultureshock #wtf #safety #toddler

After years of living in China, I’ve honestly come to see street food as better than restaurant food most of the time. Of course there are exceptions, but the best street vendors usually have a personal stake in every dish they serve. They’re cooking the same handful of specialties day after day, refining them over years, sometimes decades. There’s a sense of pride and care that’s hard to replicate in a larger restaurant. And beyond the food itself, there’s something deeply satisfying about eating on the street. No fancy décor, no presentation tricks—just great food, fresh air, and everyday life happening around you. It feels more honest, more connected to the place and the people who live there. Restaurants can offer comfort and occasion, but street food often offers something rarer: authenticity. #china #chinesefood #streetfood #familytime #chinalife

desc: Rongjiang County has just been lifted out of poverty and is a small county town on the 18th line. Rongjiang has a mild climate and abundant rainfall. mountain area. In the past few days, Rongjiang County in Qiandongnan Miao and Dong Autonomous Prefecture, Guizhou Province, which has been hit by the nationwide outbreak of "village floods", has suffered a once-in-a-decade catastrophic flood disaster. The officers and soldiers of the stationed troops in Guizhou, as well as the militia, rushed to the scene to carry out rescue operations upon hearing the order. The Rongjiang County Fire and Rescue Brigade participated in the rescue overnight, actively transferring and evacuating the distressed people through boats, ropes and other equipment in the main streets of the county At 17:00 on June 28, the Guizhou Meteorological Station announced that the heavy rainfall had weakened significantly, and the blue warning of rainstorm was lifted. It is expected that the rainfall in the Duliujiang River Basin will significantly decrease in the future, but secondary disasters still need to be prevented. ------------- Rongjiang County is under the jurisdiction of Qiandongnan Miao and Dong Autonomous Prefecture in Guizhou Province. Located in the southeastern part of Guizhou Province, in the southern part of Qiandongnan Miao and Dong Autonomous Prefecture. It borders Liping County and Congjiang County to the east, Leishan County and Sandu Shui Autonomous County to the west, Jianhe County to the north, and Libo County to the south, with a total area of 3316 square kilometers and a total population of 385000. It is a multi-ethnic mixed population county, with ethnic minorities accounting for 81% of the total population and a total of 16 ethnic groups. #Guizhou#Rongjiang#flood #cn #top #china #hot #pla #soldier

desc: China can be amazing, but there are things nobody prepares you for. You can live here for years, study, work and build a life here — but your foreign passport can still make simple things complicated. Some hotels won’t accept foreigners, some landlords don’t want foreign tenants, and the cameras are EVERYWHERE. As a student, your university can have strict rules around travel and activities. And WeChat? There are certain things you simply cannot freely post or discuss. Then there are the everyday experiences: booking a taxi and having the driver cancel after seeing you’re foreign, people staring, taking pictures without permission, touching your hair, or treating you differently because you’re Black. China has given me beautiful experiences, but also uncomfortable ones. These are the things I wish someone told me before moving here. 🇨🇳🤍 #ChinaLife #LivingInChina  #StudyInChina #lifeinchina

desc: Seven close friends in China decided to build their dream home so they could retire and live together. They found a spot in the countryside near Guangzhou and spent around 4 million yuan (about $580,000 USD) to construct a spacious and peaceful mansion surrounded by nature. They even included a tea pavilion where they can gather, drink tea, and enjoy each other's company. The idea came from a casual conversation, but they made it real by combining their savings and working closely with designers. They also made a plan for the future: they'll take care of one another as they grow older and even hire a cook and caretaker if needed.
